sections.title: Short title, extent and commencement
sections.content:
(1) This Act may be called the Administrative Tribunals Act, 1985.
(2) It extends, in so far as it relates to the Central Administrative Tribunal, to the whole of India.
(3) The provisions of this Act, in so far as they relate to the Central Administrative Tribunal, shall come into force on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint. [Came into force 1st July, 1985.]
(4) The provisions of this Act, in so far as they relate to an Administrative Tribunal for a State, shall come into force in a State on such date as the Central Government may, by notification, appoint.
amendmentNotes: Clause (b) of sub-section (2) omitted by Act 34 of 2019, s. 95 and the Fifth Schedule (w.e.f. 31-10-2019).

sections.title: Act not to apply to certain persons
amendmentNotes: Clause (b) omitted by Act 19 of 1986, s. 3 (w.e.f. 1-11-1985).
Clause (c) words 'or courts subordinate thereto' inserted by Act 51 of 1987, s. 2 (w.e.f. 22-12-1987).

sections.title: Definitions
amendmentNotes: Various clauses substituted/inserted/omitted by Acts 19 of 1986, 51 of 1987 and 1 of 2007.

sections.title: Establishment of Administrative Tribunals
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content:
(1) The Central Government shall, by notification, establish an Administrative Tribunal, to be known as the Central Administrative Tribunal, to exercise the jurisdiction, powers and authority conferred on it by or under this Act.
(2) The Central Government may, on receipt of a request from any State Government, establish, by notification, an Administrative Tribunal for that State.
(3) Two or more States may enter into an agreement that the same Administrative Tribunal shall be the Administrative Tribunal for each of the participating States, and if approved by the Central Government and published in the Gazette, the Central Government may, by notification, establish a Joint Administrative Tribunal.
(4) An agreement under sub-section (3) shall contain provisions as to the name of the Joint Administrative Tribunal, the manner of associating participating States in selecting the Chairman and other Members, the places at which Benches shall sit, apportionment of expenditure, and other supplemental, incidental and consequential provisions.
(5) The Central Government may: (a) with the concurrence of a State Government, designate Members of a State Administrative Tribunal Bench as Members of the Central Administrative Tribunal Bench for that State; or (b) on request from a State Government, designate Members of a Central Administrative Tribunal Bench functioning in a State as Members of that State's Administrative Tribunal Bench; and upon such designation the relevant Bench shall be deemed, in all respects, to be the Central or State Administrative Tribunal established under article 323A of the Constitution and this Act.
(6) Every notification under sub-section (5) shall provide for apportionment of expenditure relating to common Members and other necessary incidental provisions.
amendmentNotes: Sub-sections (5) and (6) inserted by Act 19 of 1986, s. 5 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Composition of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content:
(1) Each Tribunal shall consist of a Chairman and such number of Judicial and Administrative Members as the appropriate Government may deem fit; the jurisdiction, powers and authority of the Tribunal may be exercised by Benches thereof.
(2) Subject to the other provisions of this Act, a Bench shall consist of one Judicial Member and one Administrative Member.
(4) Notwithstanding sub-section (1), the Chairman: (a) may discharge the functions of the Judicial or Administrative Member of the Bench to which he is appointed, or of any other Bench; (b) may transfer a Member from one Bench to another; (c) may authorise the Judicial Member or Administrative Member of one Bench to also discharge functions of another Bench; and (d) may, where a case requires a Bench of more than two Members, issue general or special orders accordingly. Provided that every Bench so constituted shall include at least one Judicial Member and one Administrative Member.
(6) It shall be competent for the Chairman or an authorised Member to function as a Bench of a single Member for such classes of cases as the Chairman may specify. Provided that where a case ought to be heard by a Bench of two Members, it may be transferred accordingly.
(7) The Benches of the Central Administrative Tribunal shall ordinarily sit at New Delhi (the principal Bench), Allahabad, Calcutta, Madras, New Bombay and such other places as the Central Government may specify.
(8) The places at which the principal Bench and other Benches of a State Administrative Tribunal shall ordinarily sit shall be as the State Government may specify.
amendmentNotes: Sub-section (3) omitted and sub-sections (2), (4), (6), (7) substituted by Act 19 of 1986, s. 6 (w.e.f. 1-11-1985); further amended by Act 1 of 2007.

sections.title: Qualifications for appointment as Chairman, Vice-Chairman and other Members
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content:
(1) A person shall not be qualified for appointment as the Chairman unless he is, or has been, a Judge of a High Court. Provided that a person appointed as Vice-Chairman before the commencement of this Act shall be qualified for appointment as Chairman if he has held that office for at least two years.
(2) A person shall not be qualified for appointment: (a) as an Administrative Member, unless he has held for at least two years the post of Secretary to the Government of India (or equivalent scale) or held the post of Additional Secretary for at least five years (or equivalent scale for five years); officers on Central deputation to a lower post are deemed to have held the relevant post from the date of proforma or actual promotion; (b) as a Judicial Member, unless he is or is qualified to be a Judge of a High Court, or has held for at least two years the post of Secretary to the Government of India in the Department of Legal Affairs or the Legislative Department (including Member-Secretary, Law Commission of India), or held the post of Additional Secretary in those Departments for at least five years.
(3) The Chairman and every other Member of the Central Administrative Tribunal shall be appointed by the President after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
(4) The Chairman and every other Member of a State Administrative Tribunal shall be appointed by the President after consultation with the Governor of the concerned State.
(5) The Chairman and every other Member of a Joint Administrative Tribunal shall be appointed by the President after consultation with the Governors of the concerned States, subject to the terms of the agreement under section 4(3).
Explanation.—In computing the period during which a person has held any post, periods of holding any other post carrying the same or higher scale of pay shall be included.
amendmentNotes: Section substituted by Act 1 of 2007, s. 5 (w.e.f. 19-2-2007).

sections.title: Vice-Chairman to act as Chairman or to discharge his functions in certain circumstances
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content:
(1) On a vacancy in the office of Chairman by death, resignation or otherwise, such one of the Members as the appropriate Government may authorise shall act as Chairman until a new Chairman enters upon office.
(2) When the Chairman is unable to discharge his functions owing to absence, illness or any other cause, the Vice-Chairman (or such one of the Vice-Chairmen as the appropriate Government may authorise) shall discharge the functions of Chairman until he resumes duties.
amendmentNotes: Sub-section (1) substituted by Act 1 of 2007, s. 6 (w.e.f. 19-2-2007).

sections.title: Term of office
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content:
(1) The Chairman shall hold office for a term of five years from the date he enters upon office. Provided that no Chairman shall hold office after attaining the age of sixty-eight years.
(2) A Member shall hold office for a term of five years from the date he enters upon office, extendable by one more term of five years. Provided that no Member shall hold office after attaining the age of sixty-five years.
(3) The conditions of service of Chairman and Members shall be the same as applicable to Judges of the High Court.
amendmentNotes: Section substituted by Act 1 of 2007, s. 7 (w.e.f. 19-2-2007).

sections.title: Resignation and removal
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content:
(1) The Chairman or other Member may, by notice in writing to the President, resign his office; he shall continue in office until the expiry of three months from the date of the notice, or until a successor enters upon office, or until the expiry of his term, whichever is earliest, unless permitted by the President to relinquish office sooner.
(2) The Chairman or any other Member shall not be removed from office except by order of the President on the ground of proved misbehaviour or incapacity, after an inquiry made by a Judge of the Supreme Court in which he has been informed of the charges and given a reasonable opportunity of being heard.
(3) The Central Government may, by rules, regulate the procedure for investigation of misbehaviour or incapacity referred to in sub-section (2).
amendmentNotes: References to 'Vice-Chairman' omitted by Act 1 of 2007, s. 8 (w.e.f. 19-2-2007).

sections.title: Salaries and allowances and other terms and conditions of service of Chairman and other Members
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content: The salaries and allowances payable to, and other terms and conditions of service (including pension, gratuity and other retirement benefits) of, the Chairman and other Members shall be such as may be prescribed by the Central Government. Provided that neither the salary and allowances nor the other terms and conditions of service shall be varied to his disadvantage after appointment. Provided further that a serving Government officer appointed as a Member shall be deemed to have retired from his prior service on the date he assumed charge as Member, but his subsequent service as Member shall, at his option, be reckoned as post-retirement re-employment counting for pension and other retirement benefits in his prior service.
amendmentNotes: Second proviso inserted by Act 1 of 2007, s. 9 (w.e.f. 19-2-2007).

sections.title: Saving terms and conditions of service of Vice-Chairman
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content: The Chairman, Vice-Chairman and Member of a Tribunal appointed before the commencement of the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 2006 (1 of 2007) shall continue to be governed by the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder as if that Amendment Act had not come into force. Provided that such Chairman and Members, on completion of their term or attaining the age of sixty-five or sixty-two years (as the case may be), whichever is earlier, may, if eligible under section 8 as amended, be considered for fresh appointment in accordance with the selection procedure for such appointments, subject to the total term of the Chairman not exceeding five years and that of Members not exceeding ten years.
amendmentNotes: Inserted by Act 1 of 2007, s. 10 (w.e.f. 19-2-2007).

sections.title: Qualifications, terms and conditions of service of Chairman and Member
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content: Notwithstanding anything contained in this Act, the qualifications, appointment, term of office, salaries and allowances, resignation, removal and other terms and conditions of service of the Chairman and other Members of the Tribunal appointed after the commencement of the Tribunals Reforms Act, 2021 shall be governed by the provisions of Chapter II of that Act. Provided that the Chairman and Member appointed before the commencement of Part XIV of Chapter VI of the Finance Act, 2017 shall continue to be governed by the provisions of this Act and the rules made thereunder as if section 184 of the Finance Act, 2017 had not come into force.
amendmentNotes: Inserted by Act 7 of 2017, s. 176 (w.e.f. 26-5-2017); substituted by Act 33 of 2021, s. 15 (w.e.f. 4-4-2021).

sections.title: Provision as to the holding of offices by Chairman, etc., on ceasing to be such Chairman, etc.
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
amendmentNotes: Clauses (c) and (d) omitted by Act 1 of 2007, s. 11 (w.e.f. 19-2-2007).

sections.title: Financial and administrative powers of the Chairman
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content:
(1) The Chairman shall exercise such financial and administrative powers over the Benches as may be vested in him under rules made by the appropriate Government.
(2) The appropriate Government may designate one or more Members as Vice-Chairman(s), who shall exercise such powers and perform such functions of the Chairman as may be delegated to them by the Chairman by general or special order in writing.
amendmentNotes: Section substituted by Act 1 of 2007, s. 12 (w.e.f. 19-2-2007).

sections.title: Staff of the Tribunal
sections.subChapter: Establishment of Tribunals and Benches thereof
sections.content:
(1) The appropriate Government shall determine the nature and categories of officers and employees required to assist a Tribunal and provide the Tribunal with such staff as it thinks fit.
(1A) The officers and other employees of a Tribunal shall discharge their functions under the general superintendence of the Chairman.
(2) The salaries, allowances and conditions of service of such officers and employees shall be as specified by rules made by the appropriate Government.
amendmentNotes: Sub-section (1A) inserted by Act 19 of 1986, s. 10 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority of the Central Administrative Tribunal
sections.subChapter: Jurisdiction, Powers and Authority of Tribunals
sections.content:
(1) Save as otherwise expressly provided, the Central Administrative Tribunal shall exercise, from the appointed day, all jurisdiction, powers and authority exercisable immediately before that day by all courts (except the Supreme Court) in relation to: (a) recruitment to any All-India Service or civil service/post of the Union, or defence-connected civilian posts; (b) all service matters concerning members of any All-India Service, or persons appointed to any civil service/post of the Union, or civilians in defence services/posts, pertaining to their service in connection with the affairs of the Union, any State, or any local/other authority/corporation or society owned or controlled by the Government; (c) service matters of persons whose services have been placed by a State Government or authority at the disposal of the Central Government for appointment under clause (b). Explanation.—References to 'Union' include a Union territory.
(2) The Central Government may, by notification, apply sub-section (3) to local/other authorities and corporations or societies owned or controlled by the Government (not State-owned), with different dates permissible for different classes.
(3) From the date sub-section (2) applies to any such body, the Central Administrative Tribunal shall also exercise all jurisdiction previously exercisable by courts (except the Supreme Court) in relation to: (a) recruitment matters for such body; and (b) service matters of persons appointed to service/posts connected with such body's affairs.
amendmentNotes: Explanation to sub-section (1) inserted by Act 19 of 1986, s. 11 (w.e.f. 1-11-1985).

sections.title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority of State Administrative Tribunals
sections.subChapter: Jurisdiction, Powers and Authority of Tribunals
sections.content:
(1) Save as otherwise expressly provided, the Administrative Tribunal for a State shall exercise, from the appointed day, all jurisdiction, powers and authority exercisable immediately before that day by all courts (except the Supreme Court) in relation to: (a) recruitment to any civil service/post of the State; (b) service matters of persons (other than those covered under section 14(1)(b)) appointed to any civil service/post of the State, pertaining to service in connection with the State, local/other authority under State control, or corporation/society owned or controlled by the State; (c) service matters of persons whose services have been placed at the disposal of the State Government by such bodies for appointment under clause (b).
(2) The State Government may, by notification, apply sub-section (3) to local/other authorities and corporations or societies controlled/owned by the State, with different dates permissible for different classes.
(3) From the date sub-section (2) applies, the State Administrative Tribunal shall also exercise jurisdiction previously exercisable by courts (except the Supreme Court) in relation to recruitment and service matters connected with such bodies.
(4) For removal of doubts, the jurisdiction of a State Administrative Tribunal shall not extend to any matter within the jurisdiction of the Central Administrative Tribunal.
amendmentNotes: Amended by Act 19 of 1986, s. 12 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Jurisdiction, powers and authority of a Joint Administrative Tribunal
sections.subChapter: Jurisdiction, Powers and Authority of Tribunals
sections.content: A Joint Administrative Tribunal for two or more States shall exercise all the jurisdiction, powers and authority exercisable by the Administrative Tribunals for such States.

sections.title: Power to punish for contempt
sections.subChapter: Jurisdiction, Powers and Authority of Tribunals
sections.content: A Tribunal shall have the same jurisdiction, powers and authority in respect of contempt of itself as a High Court, and the Contempt of Courts Act, 1971 (70 of 1971) shall apply subject to modifications: (a) references to a High Court include the Tribunal; (b) references to the Advocate-General shall mean, for the Central Administrative Tribunal, the Attorney-General, Solicitor-General or Additional Solicitor-General; and for a State or Joint Administrative Tribunal, the Advocate-General of the relevant State(s).

sections.title: Distribution of business amongst the Benches
sections.subChapter: Jurisdiction, Powers and Authority of Tribunals
sections.content:
(1) Where any Benches of a Tribunal are constituted, the appropriate Government may, by notification, provide for distribution of business amongst the Benches and specify matters dealt with by each.
(2) If a question arises whether a matter falls within a Bench's allocated business, the Chairman's decision shall be final. Explanation.—"Matters" includes applications under section 19.
amendmentNotes: Amended by Act 19 of 1986, s. 13 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Applications to tribunals
sections.content:
(1) A person aggrieved by any order pertaining to a matter within the Tribunal's jurisdiction may make an application to the Tribunal for redressal of his grievance. Explanation.—"order" means an order made by the Government, local/other authority, or corporation/society owned/controlled by the Government, or by an officer, committee or body/agency thereof.
(2) Every application shall be in the prescribed form, accompanied by such documents/evidence and fee (not exceeding one hundred rupees) as prescribed by the Central Government.
(3) On receipt of an application, the Tribunal shall, if satisfied it is a fit case for adjudication, admit it; otherwise it may summarily reject the application, recording its reasons.
(4) Where an application is admitted, any pending proceeding under the relevant service rules as to redressal of grievances in relation to that matter shall abate, and no further appeal or representation shall be entertained under such rules save as otherwise directed by the Tribunal.
amendmentNotes: Sub-section (3) substituted by Act 19 of 1986, s. 14 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Applications not to be admitted unless other remedies exhausted
sections.content:
(1) A Tribunal shall not ordinarily admit an application unless satisfied that the applicant had availed of all remedies available under the relevant service rules as to redressal of grievances.
(2) A person is deemed to have availed of all such remedies: (a) if a final order rejecting the appeal/representation has been made by the competent authority; or (b) if no final order has been made and six months have expired from the date the appeal/representation was made.
(3) Any remedy by way of a memorial to the President, Governor, or other functionary shall not be deemed an available remedy unless the applicant elected to submit such memorial.

sections.title: Limitation
sections.content:
(1) A Tribunal shall not admit an application: (a) where a final order under section 20(2)(a) has been made, unless made within one year of that order; (b) where an appeal/representation under section 20(2)(b) has been made and six months have expired without a final order, unless made within one year of the expiry of that six-month period.
(2) Notwithstanding sub-section (1), where the grievance arose from an order made within the three years preceding the date the Tribunal's jurisdiction became exercisable, and no proceedings for redressal had been commenced before a High Court before that date, the application shall be entertained if made within the period under sub-section (1) or within six months of the said date, whichever is later.
(3) An application may be admitted after the periods specified in sub-sections (1) or (2) if the applicant satisfies the Tribunal of sufficient cause for the delay.

sections.title: Procedure and powers of Tribunals
sections.content:
(1) A Tribunal shall not be bound by the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 but shall be guided by principles of natural justice, and, subject to other provisions and rules, shall regulate its own procedure including place, timing, and whether to sit in public or private.
(2) A Tribunal shall decide every application as expeditiously as possible, ordinarily on a perusal of documents and written representations and after hearing such oral arguments as may be advanced.
(3) A Tribunal shall have, for discharging its functions, the same powers as a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908 while trying a suit, in respect of: (a) summoning and enforcing attendance and examination on oath; (b) discovery and production of documents; (c) receiving evidence on affidavits; (d) requisitioning public records subject to sections 123 and 124 of the Indian Evidence Act, 1872; (e) issuing commissions for examination of witnesses/documents; (f) reviewing its decisions; (g) dismissing a representation for default or deciding it ex parte; (h) setting aside orders of dismissal for default or ex parte orders; and (i) any other matter prescribed by the Central Government.
amendmentNotes: Amended by Act 19 of 1986, s. 15 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Right of applicant to take assistance of legal practitioner and of Government, etc., to appoint presenting officers
sections.content:
(1) A person making an application may appear in person or take the assistance of a legal practitioner of his choice.
(2) The Central Government, State Government, or a local/other authority/corporation/society to which section 14(3) or 15(3) applies, may authorise legal practitioners or its officers to act as presenting officers to present its case before a Tribunal.
amendmentNotes: Sub-section (2) amended by Act 19 of 1986, s. 16 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Conditions as to making of interim orders
sections.content: No interim order (by injunction, stay or otherwise) shall be made on an application unless: (a) copies of the application and supporting documents are furnished to the opposing party; and (b) that party is given opportunity to be heard. Provided that a Tribunal may dispense with these requirements as an exceptional measure, for recorded reasons, to prevent loss not adequately compensable in money, but such an interim order shall lapse after fourteen days unless the requirements are met and the Tribunal continues the order.

sections.title: Power of Chairman to transfer cases from one Bench to another
sections.content: On application by any party, after notice and hearing (or on his own motion without notice), the Chairman may transfer any case pending before one Bench to any other Bench for disposal.
amendmentNotes: Substituted, along with section 26, by Act 19 of 1986, s. 17 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Decision to be by majority
sections.content: If Members of a Bench differ in opinion, the point shall be decided by the majority opinion. If equally divided, they shall state the point(s) of difference and refer the case to the Chairman, who shall either hear the point(s) himself or refer the case for hearing by one or more other Members; such point(s) shall then be decided by the majority opinion of the Members who heard the case, including those who first heard it.

sections.title: Execution of orders of a Tribunal
sections.content: Subject to the other provisions of this Act and the rules, the order of a Tribunal finally disposing of an application or appeal shall be final and shall not be called in question in any court (including a High Court), and shall be executed in the same manner as a final order of the nature referred to in section 20(2)(a) (whether or not such final order had actually been made) would have been executed.
amendmentNotes: Amended by Act 19 of 1986, s. 18 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Exclusion of jurisdiction of courts except the Supreme Court under article 136 of the Constitution
sections.content: On and from the date a Tribunal's jurisdiction becomes exercisable in relation to recruitment or service matters, no court except (a) the Supreme Court; or (b) any Industrial Tribunal, Labour Court or other authority constituted under the Industrial Disputes Act, 1947 or corresponding law, shall have or be entitled to exercise any jurisdiction, powers or authority in relation to such recruitment or service matters.
amendmentNotes: Amended by Act 19 of 1986, s. 19 (w.e.f. 1-11-1985).

sections.title: Transfer of pending cases
sections.content:
(1) Every suit or proceeding pending before any court/authority immediately before a Tribunal's establishment, which would have fallen within the Tribunal's jurisdiction had it arisen after establishment, shall stand transferred to the Tribunal on that date. Proviso: does not apply to appeals pending before a High Court.
(2) Similarly, suits/proceedings pending before jurisdiction is conferred over any local/other authority or corporation/society shall stand transferred, subject to the same High Court appeal proviso.
(3) Where a Joint Administrative Tribunal is established for States that had State Tribunal(s), all pending cases before such State Tribunal(s) stand transferred to the Joint Administrative Tribunal.
(4) On transfer, the transferring court/authority shall forward the records, and the Tribunal may proceed with the matter from the stage reached, from an earlier stage, or de novo, as it deems fit.
(5) Where a case stands transferred to a Joint Administrative Tribunal, it may proceed from the stage reached.
(6) Every case pending before a Tribunal immediately before the commencement of the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Act, 1987, which would fall within a court's jurisdiction had it arisen after that commencement, shall stand transferred to that court.
(7) Where a case stands transferred to a court under sub-section (6), that court may proceed from the stage reached.
amendmentNotes: Amended by Acts 19 of 1986 and 51 of 1987.

sections.title: Provision for filing of certain appeals
sections.content: Where a decree or order was made by a court (other than a High Court) in a suit/proceeding before a Tribunal's establishment, being one that would have fallen within the Tribunal's jurisdiction had it arisen after establishment, and no appeal had been preferred and the limitation period for appeal had not expired before such establishment, the appeal shall lie: (a) to the Central Administrative Tribunal, within ninety days from the date the Administrative Tribunals (Amendment) Bill, 1986 received Presidential assent, or ninety days from receipt of the copy of the decree/order, whichever is later; or (b) to any other Tribunal, within ninety days of its establishment or ninety days from receipt of the copy of the decree/order, whichever is later.
amendmentNotes: Inserted by Act 19 of 1986, s. 21 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Proceedings before a Tribunal to be judicial proceedings
sections.content: All proceedings before a Tribunal shall be deemed to be judicial proceedings within the meaning of sections 193, 219 and 228 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).

sections.title: Members and staff of Tribunal to be public servants
sections.content: The Chairman and other Members, and the officers and other employees provided under section 13 to a Tribunal, shall be deemed to be public servants within the meaning of section 21 of the Indian Penal Code (45 of 1860).
amendmentNotes: Amended by Act 1 of 2007, s. 13 (w.e.f. 19-2-2007).

sections.title: Protection of action taken in good faith
sections.content: No suit, prosecution or other legal proceeding shall lie against the Central or State Government, or the Chairman or other Member of any Central, Joint or State Administrative Tribunal, or any person authorised by such Chairman or Member, for anything done or intended to be done in good faith in pursuance of this Act or any rule or order made thereunder.

sections.title: Act to have overriding effect
sections.content: The provisions of this Act shall have effect notwithstanding anything inconsistent contained in any other law for the time being in force or in any instrument having effect by virtue of any law other than this Act.

sections.title: Power to remove difficulties
sections.content:
(1) If any difficulty arises in giving effect to the provisions of this Act, the Central Government may, by order published in the Official Gazette, make such provisions, not inconsistent with this Act, as appear necessary or expedient for removing the difficulty.
(2) Every such order shall, as soon as may be, be laid before each House of Parliament.

sections.title: Power of the Central Government to make rules
sections.content:
(1) The Central Government may, subject to section 36, by notification, make rules to carry out the provisions of this Act.
(2) Such rules may provide for: (a) cases to be decided by a Bench of more than two Members under section 5(4)(d); (b) procedure for investigating misbehaviour/incapacity of the Chairman or other Member under section 9(3); (c) salaries, allowances and other terms and conditions of the Chairman and other Members; (d) the form of applications under section 19, accompanying documents/evidence, and fees for filing and for service or execution of processes; (e) rules of procedure under section 22(1) and additional matters for civil court powers under section 22(3)(i); and (f) any other prescribed matter.
amendmentNotes: Amended by Acts 19 of 1986 and 1 of 2007.

sections.title: Power of the appropriate Government to make rules
sections.content: The appropriate Government may, by notification, make rules to provide for: (a) the financial and administrative powers the Chairman may exercise over the Benches under section 12; (b) salaries, allowances and conditions of service of officers and employees of a Tribunal under section 13(2); and (c) any other matter, not specified in section 35, requiring rules by the appropriate Government.
amendmentNotes: Amended by Act 19 of 1986, s. 23 (w.e.f. 22-1-1986).

sections.title: Power to make rules retrospectively
sections.content: The power to make rules under section 35(2)(c) or section 36(b) includes the power to make such rules retrospectively from a date not earlier than the date this Act received Presidential assent, but no such retrospective rule shall prejudicially affect the interests of any person to whom it applies.
amendmentNotes: Inserted by Act 51 of 1987, s. 6 (w.e.f. 22-12-1987).

sections.title: Laying of rules
sections.content:
(1) Every rule made under this Act by the Central Government shall be laid, as soon as may be, before each House of Parliament, while in session, for a total period of thirty days (which may be comprised in one or more sessions), and if both Houses agree on a modification or that the rule should not be made, the rule shall thereafter have effect only in the modified form or be of no effect, without prejudice to anything previously done under it.
(2) Every rule made by a State Government under this Act shall be laid, as soon as may be, before the State Legislature.
